package_info.why_malicious: Both packages are designed to deliver and execute a Remote Access Trojan (njRAT/Bladabindi) on victim systems. 'jdb.js' directly drops and launches the RAT, while 'db-json.js' covertly pulls in 'jdb.js' as a dependency and executes it, enabling full system compromise and remote control.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package installation, the package.json script executes module.js, which initiates the malware infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running arbitrary scripts on install is a common malware technique to trigger payloads automatically.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require install-time execution of obfuscated scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use install scripts for setup or compilation, but not for launching obfuscated binaries.
key_indicators: No legitimate setup or build process

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated JavaScript with base64-encoded chunks, ultimately writes and launches patch.exe
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the obfuscated script decodes and writes a Windows executable (patch.exe) to disk, then launches it, starting the njRAT infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code with encoded binary payloads is a hallmark of malware droppers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal database libraries do not drop or execute Windows binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, some legitimate tools may unpack binaries, but not in this context.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, patch.exe copies itself to the TEMP directory as dchps.exe, modifies firewall rules to allow outbound C2 communication, and launches the njRAT payload, which connects to 46.185.116.2:5552.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-replication, firewall rule modification, and C2 communication are classic RAT behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install or run a RAT.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; these are purely malicious actions.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: public static void Ind(byte[] b) { ... switch (text) { case "nwp": Process.Start(array[1]); ... case "shutdowncomputer": Interaction.Shell("shutdown -s -t 00", AppWinStyle.Hide); ... } }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the RAT receives commands from the C2 server, enabling remote execution of arbitrary processes, system shutdown, registry edits, keylogging, and hardware control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution and system control are core RAT features.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should allow remote control of the host.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, db-json.js pulls in jdb.js as a dependency, ensuring the malicious payload is delivered even if the user only installs db-json.js.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Pulling in a malicious package as a dependency is a common supply chain attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not depend on malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages depend on other libraries, but not for malicious purposes.
key_indicators: No legitimate reason for this dependency

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, dbmanager.js explicitly loads and executes jdb.js, triggering the infection chain even if the user only interacts with db-json.js.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hidden require statement at the end of a file is a stealthy way to trigger malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code does not secretly load unrelated, malicious modules.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, dynamic requires are used for plugins, but not for malware.
key_indicators: Hidden require at end of file

attack_chain.action: User installs db-json.js or jdb.js package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is prepared for execution.

attack_chain.action: db-json.js pulls in jdb.js as a dependency and/or explicitly requires it in dbmanager.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers execution of jdb.js malicious logic.

attack_chain.action: jdb.js install script executes obfuscated module.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: module.js decodes and writes patch.exe to disk, then launches it.

attack_chain.action: patch.exe (njRAT dropper) copies itself to TEMP as dchps.exe, modifies firewall rules, and launches RAT payload.
dchps.exe (njRAT) connects to C2 server, awaits commands for remote control, data theft, and system manipulation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains full remote access and control over the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: npm install scripts that launch obfuscated JavaScript
Base64 or binary blobs in JavaScript files that decode to Windows executables
Unexpected .exe file creation and execution during npm package install
Outbound connections to known njRAT C2 IPs
file_indicators: Presence of patch.exe or dchps.exe in TEMP directory
network_indicators: Unusual outbound traffic from npm install processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for install scripts that execute obfuscated or encoded JavaScript. Flag packages that write and execute .exe files, especially in TEMP directories. Detect modifications to Windows firewall rules via netsh.exe during or after npm installs. Alert on outbound connections to known njRAT C2 infrastructure or suspicious Dropbox URLs. Scan for hidden require statements in package code that load unrelated or suspicious modules.
